summary: 7-phase, ~7h plan (4 waves) shipping BOTH shared tooling and a documented method. New: scripts/census-count.sh (subcommands occurrences/membership/cross-check, each emitting a record block with the verbatim producing command), scripts/tests/test-census-count.sh, scripts/tests/test-validate-no-task-references.sh, context/standards/shell-script-testing.md, context/standards/census-methodology.md. Modified: hooks/validate-no-task-references.sh separator regex + task-qualified Phase branch, manifest.json (3 provides.scripts entries), index-entries.json (2 entries). Every edit targets agent-system/extensions/core/**. Plan validator passes with 0 warnings.
decisions_made: D1: Ship both tooling and a documented method -- a prose-only deliverable cannot satisfy the binding testedness constraint.

D2: Harness location is agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/. Resolved the researcher-flagged tension with a NEW on-disk fact: core's provides.scripts ALREADY carries subdirectory-qualified paths (lint/lint-contract-compliance.sh, lint/lint-postflight-boundary.sh), so tests/ is a core-local convention, not a borrowed literature shape. Also matches literature's own scope-based split (narrow suites in tests/, broad pipeline suites flat).

D3: Helper naming inside core tests is pass()/fail()/info() with PASSED/FAILED counters, following core's existing test-task-lock-reap.sh precedent; literature's t_pass/t_fail stays valid within literature. Location is the shared rule, helper naming is extension-local. test-task-lock-reap.sh is NOT migrated (recorded as a tolerated exception in the convention doc).

D4: Fixtures are built inline via heredocs into a mktemp -d root; no committed fixture tree. Matches core's zero-committed-fixture approach and avoids registering non-script files in a provides array with no fixtures slot.

D5: Phase references are in the hook's remit ONLY in the task-qualified compound form (task N phase P / phase P of task N). A bare 'Phase 3' is explicitly OUT of remit -- it is indistinguishable from a document's own internal structure (plan-format.md, skill pipeline stages), and flagging it would cause alert fatigue on an advisory hook. This DIVERGES from the research report's recommendation to include bare Phase; the reason is stated in the plan and the decision is marked revisitable.
D6: Method doc lives at context/standards/census-methodology.md (indexed, load_when-scoped), not rules/ (auto-applied everywhere).

Candidate regex recorded for validation (not paste-blindly): '\b[Tt]asks?([[:space:]]+#?|[-_#])[0-9]+(-[0-9]+)?\b' -- explicit alternation deliberately chosen over a bracket class containing '-' to avoid the mid-class range trap.
Phase 3 includes a mutation check: reverting the separator group to [[:space:]]+ must make the suite fail. A suite that passes against the old regex is not testing anything.

Real-repo dogfooding (membership: manifest provides.scripts vs scripts/*.sh on disk) appears ONLY as a worked example in the method doc, never as a test assertion, to keep suites repo-state-independent.
